cohort: The study included all live-born children born preterm in Denmark from 1997 to 2013, totaling 70,876 children.
finding: The increasing prevalence of cerebral palsy in children born preterm was driven by the subgroup born very preterm (gestational weeks 28-31) and matched their decrease in neonatal mortality.
mod_finding: N/A (although emergency caesarean sections increased, the study concluded clinical risk factors were unlikely to explain the findings).
gest_age: All preterm births, with specific focus on very preterm (28-31 gestational weeks)
